newsitem.title: USA: Japan rice, Sino-U.S. food swap urged for N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Japan rice, Sino-U.S. food swap urged for N.Korea.

text.p: The threat of starvation in North Korea could be reduced sharply if Japan donated some of its rice hoard and the United States worked with China to speed delivery of food aid, food aid experts said on Thursday.
"We are running out of time," warned Andrew Natsios, vice president of the World Vision U.S. The charity says famine could begin in late May or early June.
North Korea faces a food shortage of more than one million metric tons this year, according to experts.

Earlier this week, the United States pledged 50,000 tons of corn to a U.N. World Food Programme request for 200,000 tons of food aid for North Korea to relieve flood losses. An earlier U.S. donation of 27,000 tons was en route by sea. It would take about two months to deliver the corn.

"In three months, there will be mass starvation," Natsios said at a news conference. He suggested a food swap in which China would provide the 50,000 tons of corn now and accept the U.S. shipment to replenish its supplies.
"We urge the World Food Programme and the U.S. government to consider a food swap," Natsios said.

Representative Tony Hall, who visited North Korea earlier this month, suggested Japan could donate surplus rice for famine relief. Japan has about 250,000-350,000 tons of old rice that has little potential for domestic consumption, he said.
"According to a lot of witnesses, it is rotting. Japan could let it go, at least a portion of it," said Hall, an Ohio Democrat and longtime voice for hunger prevention.
Hall suggested that a famine fund could be created in Japan to receive donations of surplus rice if direct contributions to North Korea were difficult. Japan and North Korea have bitter disputes.
Natsios applauded the idea of using surplus Japanese rice for hunger relief.
Officials at the Agency for International Development, the U.S. agency making the food donations, were not immediately available to discuss the food swap idea.
